fact_schema.timestamp: ISO 8601 datetime — when the fact was RECORDED (ingestion time)
fact_schema.provenance: owner_stated|agent_inferred|tool_derived — trust tier of the fact's origin; see storage.VALID_PROVENANCE. Missing on facts written before this field existed, treated as trusted by storage.is_trusted_provenance()
fact_schema.valid_from: ISO 8601 datetime — when the fact became TRUE (event time). Defaults to timestamp when the caller doesn't know a more specific event date; can differ from timestamp (e.g. a fact recorded days after the event it describes)
fact_schema.valid_to: ISO 8601 datetime|null — when the fact stopped being true. Null while active; stamped by supersede_fact() when replaced. Together with valid_from, lets storage.facts_valid_at() answer 'what was true as of date X' even for since-superseded facts, which read_entity()'s active-only filter can't reconstruct

notes: V1 fields (content, type, extracted, active) kept for backward compatibility
V2 fields (fact, category, context, timestamp, source, status, supersededBy) are canonical
provenance and valid_from/valid_to are additive fields on top of V2 — both optional on read (missing on any fact written before they existed), always written on new facts
Both schemas read correctly by storage.py
